newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin says budget revenues improved.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin says budget revenues improved.

text.p: Russian government revenues improved in March and April, but are still well below plan and the government must cut spending to restore order to public finances, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Wednesday.

"The situation in March and April has improved somewhat, but this is still not conclusive," he told the the State Duma lower house of parliament. "We have no reason to hope that the situation will improve by itself."
Chernomyrdin said revenues in the first four months of this year were running at only 64.6 percent of budgeted levels, while expenditure was 70 percent of plan.
The 1997 budget says the government must propose spending cuts, or sequestration, to the Duma if revenues fall below 90 percent of budgeted levels in any quarter.
First Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov is due to present a sequestration bill to the Duma later on Wednesday, although many deputies have already signalled their opposition to the plans.
